blocks.x: We also picked up two other things in the Meeker book. That is that you didn't appear in any more movies, but you were heard in two more movies.

Now, I don't have that information with me, but I'm going to dig it up. One of them was a -- I guess it was a short -- what you call a short subject.
And in one of them, it features the music of Benny Carter, and you sing a song in it. Perhaps that -- I think that was 1941. That would be when you were on tour perhaps with the Benny Carter --

Yeah, it must've been. Those selections were done for, what at that time, a box -- I don't even know what you call it -- in which you can insert a coin and see the picture and see the performance and hear the songs too.
There were quite a few of them made, but the box was not that successful. And so they took it off the market.
There were some other soundies made at the same time that I happened to see. In fact, they did -- the Mills Brothers did one -- Paper Doll. And they used Dorothy Dandridge as the

Right. So those soundies -- I think I did a couple. St. Louis Blues is one -- I forget the other one. I had made a couple of things with Benny then. Those selections and I had a couple of vocals on a record date that Benny made too.
